faq.a: A high-yield savings account usually pays a higher annual percentage yield (APY) than a standard savings account. Enter the APY yourself — this tool does not fetch, show, or recommend any bank's rate, and rates change over time.
faq.q: What is a high-yield savings account?

faq.a: APY is the yearly rate of return on your savings, including the effect of compounding. This calculator compounds monthly: each month's interest is added to your balance, so the next month earns interest on a slightly larger balance.
faq.q: What is APY, and how does compounding work here?

faq.a: It depends on the APY your bank actually pays, which can change. This tool shows what your balance would be if the APY you enter stayed the same for the whole period — treat it as a projection, not a promise.
faq.q: Will my savings really grow by this much?

faq.a: Some accounts require a minimum balance or limit withdrawals. Check the account terms with the bank before you open one — this calculator only does the math.
faq.q: Are there limits on high-yield savings accounts?

whenNotToUse: This tool does not fetch or show any bank's rate — the APY is entered by you, and real rates change, so the result is a projection, not a guarantee.
It assumes the same APY and the same monthly contribution for the whole period; real accounts and real budgets change.
It does not account for taxes on interest earned or for fees — check both before relying on the numbers.
